title: Microsoft Teams: report a message or an external user for a security concern in US Government clouds
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the documented reporting controls. It explicitly preserves Microsoft's conflicting Government-cloud availability statements and distinguishes the published general reporting requirements from the still-undocumented Government rollout details.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Government-cloud users reporting suspicious messages within Teams.
claims.quote: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Government-cloud users reporting external users within Teams.
claims.quote: Users in Gov clouds can now report suspicious messages and external users within Teams.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Reports surface in the Teams admin center for administrators to investigate and act on.
claims.quote: Reports are surfaced in the Teams admin center, giving admins greater visibility into potentially malicious activity and enabling them to investigate and take appropriate action.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default or arrival behaviour specifically for this Government-cloud rollout.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Report a security concern GCC GCC High DoD default; Teams Gov security concern default. Opened end-user-reporting-security and submissions-teams: general Teams default is On, but no Gov rollout default; the latter excludes Gov reporting. Roadmap gives no default.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Defender entitlement through add-on licences or subscriptions containing it.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2 (add-on licenses or included in subscriptions like Microsoft 365 E5), admins can also see user reported messages in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Teams feature page frames reporting for organisations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Defender reporting page lists Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Entitlement specifically for the new Government-cloud reporting rollout is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams report a security concern price licensing government; Teams user reported GCC licensing price meter. Opened submissions-teams, end-user-reporting-security, submissions-admin and mdo-gov: general Defender offers are published, not this new Gov reporting entitlement.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price or meter specifically for this feature in Government clouds.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user reported GCC licensing price meter; Teams report a security concern price licensing government. Opened submissions-teams, submissions-admin, end-user-reporting-security and mdo-gov; none publishes a price or meter for this Gov reporting feature.

claims.claim: The cited page gives Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Report a security concern.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Messaging policies.
3. Select a policy.
4. Turn on the setting: Report a security concern.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting $true enables security-concern reporting for the selected messaging policy.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet updates a Teams messaging policy.
### -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting
This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False

claims.claim: The report is reached through Teams admin center > Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports.
2. On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.

claims.claim: No API or automated export feed for the User reported security submissions report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: User reported security submissions API PowerShell; Teams user reported security submissions report API PowerShell Microsoft Graph export. Opened report page, submissions-teams, Graph beta threatSubmission: no report API; threatSubmission covers email, attachments and URLs.

claims.claim: Viewing or configuring user reporting in the Teams admin center requires Global Administrator or Teams Administrator.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator* or Teams Administrator roles.

claims.claim: The newer experience locates this policy under Settings & policies.
claims.quote: To access this policy in the new experience, go to Settings & policies.

claims.claim: Cloud availability for the messaging-policy setting itself is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Report a security concern GCC GCC High DoD default; Teams Gov security concern default. Opened end-user-reporting-security, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and submissions-teams: no cloud matrix for the setting; Gov reporting exclusion is separately stated.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and scope; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The user's messaging-policy Report a security concern setting controls reporting of chat and channel messages and external users.
claims.quote: For chat and channel messages and external users, the Report a security concern setting must be turned on in the user's messaging policy.

claims.claim: A user reports a chat or channel message through ... > Report this message > Security concern.
claims.quote:
Go to chat or channel message and select … > Report this message.
2. Select Security concern.

claims.claim: The Defender instructions label the message-reporting choice Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content.
claims.quote: In the report this message dialog that opens, verify Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content is selected, and then select Report.

claims.claim: Turning off Communication Compliance reporting can replace the selection dropdown with a confirmation pop-up.
claims.quote: If reporting for Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance is turned off, users might not have the dropdown list to select Security risk - Spam, phishing, malicious content. Instead, they're shown a confirmation pop-up.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users can report an external user by selecting Report this person while blocking them from an external chat request.
claims.quote:
Open the external chat request.
2. Select Block, Delete or Leave, depending on the chat type and your organization's settings, and follow the prompt to block the user.
3. Click Report this person checkbox and confirm.

claims.claim: Users can also select Report this person when blocking an external contact from the user's profile card.
claims.quote:
Open the user's profile card.
2. Open the menu option and select Block contact
3. Click Report this person checkbox and confirm.

claims.quote: User reporting of calls, meetings, and messages in Teams is not supported in U.S. Government organizations (Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, and DoD).

claims.claim: That Defender Government-cloud exclusion note does not mention reporting external users.
claims.quote: User reporting of calls, meetings, and messages in Teams is not supported in U.S. Government organizations (Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High, and DoD).

| Report | Public | GCC | GCCH | DoD | What's measured? |

claims.quote: submissions-teams HTML: updated_at="2026-10-05T22:34:00Z"; teams-reporting-reference HTML: updated_at="2026-08-13T22:44:00Z". Roadmap record: "modified": "2026-11-12T01:50:56".

claims.claim: The chats-and-channels CSV includes a sender-domain field.
claims.quote:
Sender domain name | Domain of the sender. This field might be blank if the sender uses a consumer account, depending on their privacy setting.
Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.claim: The chats-and-channels CSV participant list contains at most 20 entries.
claims.quote: List of participants in the conversation, including their display name, email address, and Microsoft Resource Identifier (MRI). Maximum 20 entries: up to 10 entries from the reporter's tenant and up to 10 entries from non-reporter tenants.

claims.claim: The exported CSV includes optional reporter comments.
claims.quote:
Reporter comments | Optional comments that the reporter user sent along with the report, if any.
Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.claim: The User report includes the reported user's display name and email address if available.
claims.quote: Reported user's display name and email address, if available. If the reported user uses a consumer account, their email address might not be available depending on their privacy setting.

claims.claim: The Defender documentation says reporting a Teams item to Microsoft copies associated message content for analysis.
claims.quote:
When a user reports a Teams item to Microsoft, the following data associated with the item is copied and included in ongoing algorithm reviews, as applicable:
- Message content.

claims.claim: Up to fifteen messages before and after the reported message might also be shared for analysis.
claims.quote: The submission might also include contextual data for the reported message. Specifically, up to fifteen messages before and after the reported message might also be shared for analysis.

claims.claim: Whether Government reports share that specific surrounding-message context is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams security reports Government data shared messages. Opened security-report-privacy and submissions-teams. Privacy confirms sharing report data generally, not the fifteen-message context in Gov; submissions-teams gives that context but excludes Gov reporting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Reporting is initiated by a user.
claims.quote: Users who see a concerning chat or a channel message in Teams can report it as a security risk.

claims.claim: The admin report provides organisation-level review of security reports submitted by users.
claims.quote: The User reported security submissions report in the Microsoft Teams admin center helps you review security-related reports submitted by users in your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Users can report the same item multiple times.
claims.quote: Users can report the same items multiple times.

claims.claim: Not a security concern is the reporting option for messages users believe were incorrectly flagged.
claims.quote:
Users can report messages in Teams chats or channels that are incorrectly flagged by Link Protection as containing malicious URLs.
In the report dialog that opens, select Not a security concern.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Defender supports user reporting of messages but not yet of external users; external-user reports are reviewed in the Teams admin center instead.
claims.quote: Only user reporting of messages is supported in Microsoft Defender as of now. User reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.

claims.claim: The report page's prerequisites name reporting settings, not a licence requirement.
claims.quote:
Reported interactions appear in the User reported security submissions reports only after users submit reports.
Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Message reporting has separate Teams admin center and Defender portal settings.
claims.quote:
'Report a security concern' reporting of messages and users in Teams is made of two separate settings:
- In the Teams admin center
- In the Microsoft Defender portal

claims.claim: The Defender setting must also be on for user-reported messages to appear correctly on Submissions > User reported.
claims.quote: If "Report a security concern" is turned on in the Teams admin center, it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported messages to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.claim: Microsoft states that report data is also shared with Microsoft for threat analysis and service protection.
claims.quote: Report data is also shared with Microsoft for threat analysis and service protection.
